newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU ministers break off EMU pact talks-diplomat.
newsitem.headline: EU ministers break off EMU pact talks-diplomat.

text.p: European Union finance ministers broke off talks on a stability pact to protect the planned single currency on Thursday night but may resume later, an EU diplomat said.

"They've taken a short break and will come back to discuss the legal status of the euro," the diplomat told Reuters. He was referring to another aspect of the EU's plans to launch a monetary union in 1999.

The legal framework is aimed at helping to ensure financial market contracts remain valid after economic and monetary union (EMU) and at providing details which financial institutions need to prepare for for the launch of the euro.

The diplomat said Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn would have to decide whether to resume talks on the stability pact or end the session. He noted the possibility of the ministers going into a "restricted session", a higher level of debate.

There was a widespread view that Germany's proposals were not in line with the Maastricht Treaty, the basis of the EMU plan. The stability pact is aimed at enforcing fiscal discipline after monetary union.
